skills.name: Operations in the set of integers

note.text:
The integers are the natural numbers and their opposites: …, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, … The set of integers is written ℤ. On the number line, numbers get bigger to the right, so −2 > −5.
Adding: same signs, add the sizes and keep the sign: −4 + (−3) = −7. Different signs, subtract the smaller size from the larger and keep the sign of the larger: −9 + 4 = −5.
Subtracting a number is adding its opposite: 3 − (−5) = 3 + 5 = 8.
Multiplying and dividing: same signs give a positive answer, different signs a negative one: (−6) × (−2) = 12, (−12) ÷ 3 = −4.
Multiply and divide before you add and subtract.

worked_example.problem: The temperature in a cold room is {t} °C. It falls by {f} °C, then rises by {r} °C. What is the final temperature?
steps: Rising by {r} °C means adding: {t - f} + {r} = {t - f + r} °C.
worked_example.answer: The final temperature is {t - f + r} °C.

cards.idea: The integers are the whole numbers and their opposites. On the number line, the number further to the right is greater.
example: −{a} is to the right of −{b}, so −{a} > −{b}.
{z} > −{c}: every positive number is greater than every negative number.

misconceptions.explain: On the number line {max(a, b)} is to the right of {min(a, b)}, so it is greater. Of two negative numbers, the one closer to zero is greater.

solution: On the number line, {max(a, b)} is to the right of {min(a, b)}.

cards.idea: Adding integers: with the same signs, add the sizes and keep the sign. With different signs, subtract the smaller size from the larger and keep the sign of the larger.
example: {c} + {d} = {c + d} (different signs: {abs(c)} − {d} = {abs(c) - d}, and {abs(c)} is the larger size).

cards.idea: Subtracting a number is the same as adding its opposite.
Multiplying or dividing two integers: same signs give a positive answer; different signs give a negative answer.

misconceptions.explain: The signs are different, so subtract the sizes: the answer is {a + b}.
Check the sign. {a < 0 == b < 0 ? 'Both numbers have the same sign, and the answer keeps it.' : 'The answer takes the sign of the number with the larger size.'}
The signs are different, so subtract the sizes instead of adding them.

solution: {a < 0 == b < 0 ? 'Same signs: add the sizes and keep the sign.' : 'Different signs: subtract the smaller size from the larger, and keep the sign of the larger size.'}

misconceptions.explain: Check the sign of your answer: {a} + {br(-b)} = {a - b}.

solution: Subtracting {br(b)} is the same as adding its opposite, {br(-b)}.

misconceptions.explain: Check the sign: {signWord(a)} × {signWord(b)} gives a {signWord(a * b)} answer.

solution: {a < 0 == b < 0 ? 'Same signs, so the answer is positive.' : 'Different signs, so the answer is negative.'}

misconceptions.explain: Check the sign: {signWord(c)} ÷ {signWord(b)} gives a {signWord(q)} answer.

solution: {q < 0 ? 'Different signs, so the answer is negative.' : 'Same signs, so the answer is positive.'}

questions.prompt: At 6 a.m. the temperature at the top of Mount Cameroon was {t} °C. By noon it had risen by {r} °C. What was the temperature at noon?

misconceptions.explain: The temperature rose, so add {r}: {t} + {r} = {t + r}.
{t} is below zero. Count up {r} from {t}: {t} + {r} = {t + r}.
Multiplication and division come before addition: work out {a} × {br(b)} and {br(c)} ÷ {br(d)} first.
Check the sign of {br(c)} ÷ {br(d)}: it is {e}.

solution: Multiply and divide first: {a} × {br(b)} = {a * b} and {br(c)} ÷ {br(d)} = {e}.
